title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap & Pricing (Integrated) - 2026-03-04
author: Ava Chen
summary: Comprehensive product document that consolidates the Unified Inference product overview, PRD-level requirements, component design specs, roadmap & themes for the next three quarters, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for the March 2026 release. This doc is intended for product, engineering, sales enablement, and GTM stakeholders as the single source of truth for upcoming rolls and customer-facing messaging.
body:
Overview

This document describes the Unified Inference product: a single developer-facing runtime and control plane offering consistent API, cost controls, and rollout tooling across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Unified Inference bundles the Redwood serving runtime, smart routing, and Redwood Optimize cost/performance toolkit under one product umbrella.

Goals and success criteria

1) Adoption: 25% of new API signups in Q2 2026 adopt Unified Inference sandbox flows.
2) Performance: median text-generation tail latency (p95) <= 220ms for 512-token requests on Hosted tier for curated models.
3) Cost efficiency: 10-20% unit cost reduction for workloads using recommended batching/quantization profiles from Redwood Optimize.
4) Enterprise readiness: complete Private deployment checklist including KMS integration and audit logging for 3 pilot customers by end of Q3 2026.

Target personas

- ML/Infra Engineer: needs predictable latency and tools to tune throughput.
- Product Engineer: wants simple API and clear pricing.
- Platform/Cloud Architect: needs VPC/on-prem packaging and compliance artefacts.

Product scope (what's in/out)

Included in scope for March 2026:
- Unified API surface: text generation, chat, embeddings, and function/tool calling with identical request/response semantics across deployment modes.
- Redwood Optimize v2 integrations: automated batching suggestions, model quantization recommendations, and caching policies.
- Smart routing: policy-based routing (latency/cost/region) with automatic compatible fallback.
- Console updates: per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and rollout UI for canary/ABs.

Out of scope for March 2026:
- Full model training lifecycle (model building, fine-tuning workflows).
- Multi-cloud dedicated capacity (initial Dedicated offering limited to our primary cloud provider).

Key user journeys and requirements (PRD-level)

1) Onboard and test a model variant (self-serve sandbox)
- Requirement: Developer can spin up a sandbox endpoint with a curated model in < 10 minutes.
- Success criteria: 95% of test sandboxes provision in < 10 minutes during business hours.
- Acceptance tests: API call returns a valid streaming response within SLOs.

2) Configure a rollout (canary -> gradual -> full)
- Requirement: Console must support a 3-stage rollout with traffic split config, automatic rollback on regression, and health checks.
- SLOs: Canary duration default 30 minutes; rollback threshold = 2x error rate over baseline or latency p95 > 350ms for more than 5 minutes.

3) Apply cost/performance recommendations
- Requirement: Redwood Optimize provides per-route recommendations (batch_size, quantization_profile, cache_policy) and expected unit-cost delta.
- UI: Show \"apply\" button with preview of expected latency and cost change.

4) Private deployment checklist (enterprise)
- Requirement: Private control plane plus data plane within customer VPC, KMS support, audit logging pushed to customer SIEM, and upgrade/rollback playbook.
- Acceptance: Pilot customer completes deployment and passes security review.

Design specifications (high level)

Components:
- API Gateway (redwood-api): request validation, rate limiting, token accounting. Owner: eng-platform.
- Router Service (redwood-router): policies for latency/cost/region routing, fallback mapping to compatible model variants. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- Serving Runtime (redwood-runtime): GPU-optimized inference engine with continuous batching, KV-cache management, and quantization execution paths. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- Optimize Engine (redwood-optimize): offline/online evaluator that suggests batching/quantization/cache settings. Owner: applied-ml-and-evals.
- Console (redwood-console): dashboards, rollout UI, cost breakdowns. Owner: eng-developer-experience.

APIs and request model

API surface will remain backwards-compatible with existing Redwood API. Key additions:
- POST /v1/rollouts - create canary/AB rollout with traffic split rules.
- POST /v1/recommendations/apply - apply Optimize recommendations to a route.

Example request (streaming, text-generation):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b-v2", "input":"Summarize the production playbook", "max_tokens":256, "stream":true}'

Configuration YAML example (route override):

route: my-chat-route
overrides:
  batching:
    max_batch_size: 32
    max_latency_ms: 50
  quantization_profile: q4_0
  cache_policy: prefix_kv_cache

Operational SLOs and thresholds

- Availability (Hosted API): 99.9% monthly uptime.
- Latency: p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 220ms (512 tokens) for curated models on Hosted standard tier.
- Error rate: API error rate (5xx + 4xx-unexpected) < 1% per route.
- Rollout rollback threshold: 2x baseline error rate OR p95 latency spike > 350ms for > 5 minutes.

Roadmap & themes (Q2 2026 - Q4 2026)

Q2 2026 (current scope - March release)
- Launch Unified API + Redwood Optimize v2 recommendations.
- Console: rollout UI + per-route cost breakdown.
- Pilot Private deployments with 2 enterprise customers.

Q3 2026
- Expand Dedicated availability with multi-AZ capacity pools.
- Gated auto-scaling policies and burst capacity options.
- Quality guardrails: automated eval regressions with alerting.

Q4 2026
- Multi-cloud Dedicated support; expanded model catalog with 3rd-party verified profiles.
- Advanced SLOs: per-customer latency SLAs and cross-region failover.

Roadmap milestones and dependencies

- Milestone: Route-based rollouts GA. Dependent on: redwood-router health checks and console rollout UI. Target: 2026-04-15.
- Milestone: Private deployment pilot complete. Dependent on: KMS/HSM integration, IaC packaging. Target: 2026-06-30.
- Milestone: Dedicated multi-AZ beta. Dependent on: capacity planner and autoscaler. Target: 2026-09-15.

Pricing & packaging notes

Principles:
- Clear unit economics: separate compute (per-token) and provisioned capacity (Dedicated reservations).
- PLG-friendly free tier: small monthly token allowance + sandbox endpoints.
- Enterprise add-ons: extended retention, compliance packages, premium SLAs.

Proposed tiers (summary):
- Free (Developer sandbox): 50k tokens/month, limited concurrency, no SLA.
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): per-token pricing differentiated by model family and quantization profile. Streaming billed per token emitted.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly/annual commits priced by GPU-hour equivalent with overage pricing. Includes isolation guarantees and standard SLA.
- Private (enterprise): Platform license + optional support tier. Pricing based on node count and deployment complexity.

Example pricing table (guidance only)

- redwood-7b-v2 (float16): $0.0008 / input token, $0.0012 / output token (Hosted)
- redwood-7b-v2 (q4_0): 30% cost reduction compared to float16 with expected ~10% median latency increase.
- Dedicated reserved GPU-hour: $X / GPU-hour (negotiated per contract)

Packaging notes for sales

- Emphasize predictable performance guarantees for Dedicated and Private tiers.
- Provide cost-savings case studies from Redwood Optimize recommendations (avg 14% cost reduction across pilot customers).
- Offer migration playbook for customers moving from Hosted to Dedicated/Private with estimated downtime, rollback steps, and test checklist.

Release notes: March 2026 (v2026-03-04)

What's new:
- Unified API: GA for text generation, chat, embeddings, and tool-calling across Hosted and Dedicated alpha.
- Redwood Optimize v2: per-route recommendations for batching and quantization with preview and apply flows.
- Rollouts: Console supports canary AB flows with automatic rollback policy.
- Cost dashboards: token-level breakdowns visible in Console and via /v1/usage API.

Known issues & mitigation:
- Private deployment initial images require manual configuration for some KMS providers (tracked: INF-2743). Mitigation: runbook published and eng-private-deployments on-call for pilot installs.
- Some quantized profiles show higher tail latency for long-sequence (>2k tokens) workloads (known: PERF-3178). Mitigation: Optimize recommends float16 fallback for long sequences and runtime implements automatic fallback when p95 exceeds threshold.

Rollout plan and migration steps

1) Internal canary (1 week): enable new features for internal Redwood tenants and run synthetic load. Owners: eng-serving-runtime, eng-platform.
2) Pilot customers (2-6 weeks): select 2-3 customers (one SaaS, one enterprise, one platform) for guided onboarding. Owner: Customer Success + Solutions Eng.
3) Gradual GA: enable for 10% of new signups, monitor SLOs for 2 weeks, then increase to 100%.

Monitoring and telemetry

- Metrics to track: per-route QPS, p50/p95/p99 latency, token usage by model, cache hit ratio, rollout error rate, recommendation apply rate.
- Dashboards: pre-built Grafana dashboards in eng-platform; Console surfaces high-level KPIs for product & sales.

Appendices

A. Rollout health check example (pseudo-SQL):
SELECT route, count(*) AS errors, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status < 500) AS ok, error_rate = errors::float / (errors+ok)
FROM request_logs
WHERE time > now() - interval '30 minutes' AND route = 'my-chat-route'
GROUP BY route;

B. Upgrade & rollback playbook (summary):
- Pre-check: backup KV caches, snapshot model weights registry, validate compatibility matrix.
- Upgrade order: redwood-runtime (canary nodes) -> redwood-router -> redwood-api -> console.
- Rollback: toggle routing policy back to previous model variant and abort in-progress rollouts; restore caches from snapshot if necessary.
